body:
Renee Sullivan: heads up — potential last-minute SDK breaking change risk for demo. I saw chatter about `redwood` JS SDK + Python SDK changes landing this week. If that ships before our demos, we could get brittle live steps (streaming + tool calling). Can we pin versions for the demo tenant / demo app and add a quick “upgrade note” in the internal demo guide?

Monica Patel: yep, good call. We have a minor version bump queued that changes a couple response fields + streaming event names in the TS SDK. It *should* be backward compatible via adapters, but I don’t want to bet a live demo on “should”.

Alex Martinez: +1 to pinning. For the sales demo app we can hard pin both:
- npm package.json
- python requirements
Also we should pin the OpenAI-compat client wrapper version if we’re using it anywhere.

Markus Klein: please do. We had a live demo last month where streaming behaved differently than expected (client parsing issue). If we can freeze the demo app deps, I can stop sweating surprise behavior.

Renee Sullivan: what versions are “known good” right now? I have the demo app locally on:
- `@redwood-ai/sdk` currently floating on `^0.8.x`
- python `redwood-inference` floating on `>=0.7`
If we pick exact versions, I’ll update the demo repo + scenario runner.

Monica Patel: recommend:
- TS: `@redwood-ai/sdk@0.8.3`
- Python: `redwood-inference==0.7.9`
Those are what the docs examples + integration tests ran against last week.
The risky one is the TS `0.9.0` (new streaming event shape + renamed `tool_calls` parsing helper).

Alex Martinez: cool. Proposed changes:
1) Demo app `package.json`:
```json
{
  "dependencies": {
    "@redwood-ai/sdk": "0.8.3"
  }
}
```
(no caret)

2) Python demo scripts `requirements.txt`:
```
redwood-inference==0.7.9
```

3) Add a short note to the internal demo guide:
- “Demo app dependencies are intentionally pinned. Do not `npm update` / `pip install -U` before a customer call.”
- “If you need newer SDK features, follow the upgrade checklist + run scenario runner.”

Elliot Price: I can add the upgrade note in the internal guide + link to the runbook section (“validate streaming + tool calling outputs”). Where should the canonical pinned versions live — in the demo repo README or in Confluence too?

Markus Klein: both. README for whoever is running the app. Confluence for enablement / certification (so people don’t “clean up deps” the night before).

Renee Sullivan: + we should add a quick “if you *must* upgrade” checklist:
- run scenario runner `demo run core-api` (streaming, structured output, tool calling)
- verify outputs match expected snapshots
- verify Console dashboard events still show up (synthetic traffic generator unaffected)

Monica Patel: also worth calling out *what changes* in 0.9.0 so people don’t get confused:
- streaming emits `response.delta` instead of `token.delta`
- tool call args now come through as parsed JSON by default (previously string)
So demo scripts that do string concatenation can break.

GitHub Bot: PR opened by alexmartinez: redwood-examples#214 “Pin demo SDK versions and add upgrade note”

Alex Martinez: PR includes:
- pin TS + python deps
- add `DEMO_SDK_PINNED.md` with rationale + upgrade steps
Renee, can you sanity check the scenario runner still passes on your end?

Renee Sullivan: yup will do in ~30 mins. I’ll also update the talk track “backup mode” callout so SEs know to avoid upgrading on the fly.

Elliot Price: I’ll add a section to the internal demo guide:
“SDK Version Pinning (Why / How / When to Upgrade)” and include the exact versions Monica recommended.

Markus Klein: thank you. This is exactly the kind of thing that kills confidence during demos.

Monica Patel: once 0.9.0 is out and stable, we can schedule a deliberate demo upgrade (with one dry run + recorded backup). For now, pin + ship.

Renee Sullivan: sounds good. I’ll reply here once I’ve validated core scenario outputs w/ the pinned versions.
